summary.title: Disagreement with sister about Dad's driving
summary.what_happened: My dad is 84. Last month he scraped the garage door, and two weeks ago he got lost driving to a shop he has used for 20 years. My sister Eeva does not agree that he should stop driving. She lives near him and drives him to many things. I live 300 km away. She says taking the car would take away his independence and that he would get depressed. She also says I don't see him enough to judge. No doctor has assessed his driving or memory yet.
summary.my_feelings: I am worried that someone could get hurt. I feel my concerns are being dismissed.
summary.my_needs: I need us to take his driving safety seriously and to act before an accident happens.
summary.desired_outcome: I want us to take the keys this weekend before someone gets hurt.

consult.text:
It sounds like you are frightened for your dad and for other people, and also frustrated that Eeva seems to wave away what you have seen. That is a heavy place to be, especially from 300 km away.

Eeva may see this differently. She is the one who spends time with him and drives him around, so she sees daily how much the car means to his freedom. She may fear that losing it would hurt him, and she may feel her work is being overlooked when you say you don't see him enough to judge.

One thing that may have made this harder is the plan to take the keys this weekend. Doing it quickly and without her agreement could feel to her like being overruled, and could also feel humiliating to your dad. Your safety worry is serious, though. A scraped door and getting lost on a familiar route are real signs, and it is fair to act on them.

What is unknown is the cause. No doctor has assessed his driving or memory, so nobody knows how serious this is.

Some next steps: ask for a doctor's driving and memory assessment, and tell Eeva you both want the same thing, which is Dad safe and still independent. Talk with her about other ways he can get around, such as taxis or rides. And ask Dad what he thinks too.
But if he kills someone, it's on us. Why should I wait?

I hear how much fear is behind that, and it is a reasonable fear. Your worry about safety is not wrong, and I am not telling you to ignore it.

What I would gently question is the choice between taking the keys this weekend and doing nothing. Those are not the only two options. A medical assessment can often be booked fairly quickly, and it would give you both something neutral to rely on, instead of her opinion against yours. If the doctor finds a problem, it becomes much harder for anyone to argue that he should keep driving.

I also still think how you do this matters. If Eeva feels pushed aside, she may resist more, and that could delay things more than a few days of planning would. Dad has a say in this as well.

In the meantime, you could ask Eeva to ride with him and tell you what she sees, or ask whether he can avoid longer or unfamiliar trips until the assessment. Which of these feels possible to suggest to her this week?

share_draft: Hi Eeva. I have been worried about Dad's driving since he scraped the garage door last month and got lost on the way to a shop he has used for 20 years. I know you see him much more than I do, and I understand you worry that losing the car would take away his independence and make him low. I also know I live far away, so I may be missing things. I need us to take the safety side seriously before someone gets hurt. Could we talk about it this week? I would like to hear how it looks to you, and maybe we could ask a doctor to assess his driving and memory together.
